text:
FOOTNOTES

1/ Before spending any schools for the deaf and the blind fund monies in excess of \$12,955,500 in fiscal year 2026-2027, the Arizona state schools for the deaf and the blind shall report to the joint legislative budget committee the intended use of the monies. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

2/ Before spending any cooperative services fund monies in excess of \$15,346,300 in fiscal year 2026-2027, the Arizona state schools for the deaf and the blind shall report to the joint legislative budget committee the intended use of the monies. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

3/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Program. The amount for the Administration/Statewide program is the Operating Lump Sum, with the other programs appropriated as Special Line Items in addition to the School Bus/Agency Vehicle Replacement.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$38,131,600 and 562.2 FTE Positions in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts consist of:

General Fund \$25,176,100

Schools for the Deaf and the Blind Fund 12,955,500

Adjustments are as follows:

Base Adjustment

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,442,100) from the ASDB Fund in FY 2027 for a base adjustment reflecting lower-than-anticipated revenues compared with the enacted budget. The FY 2026 enacted budget assumed the ASDB fund would receive total revenues of \$14,156,500 from special education vouchers and state land trust endowment earnings. The FY 2027 Baseline assumes that actual revenues into the ASDB Fund in FY 2026 will be \$12,714,400, or \$(1,442,100) less than the appropriated amount. This estimate assumes that caseloads in ASDB's site-based programs would remain at the October 2025 level of 382. This adjustment is partly attributable to the decrease in land trust endowment revenues, as the distribution rate reverted to 2.5% from 6.9% in accordance with the requirements of Proposition 123.

Enrollment

The Baseline includes no net funding change from the Schools for the Deaf and the Blind (ASDB) Fund in FY 2027 for enrollment. The budget assumes that enrollment in ASDB site-based programs remains unchanged from FY 2026 and therefore includes no funding increase or decrease for enrollment changes for ASDB for FY 2027.

Inflation

The Baseline includes an increase of \$244,900 from the ASDB Fund in FY 2027 for a 2.0% increase to the Base Level component of the Special Education voucher formula. A.R.S. § 15-901.01 requires annual increases for inflation in the per pupil “base level” in the Basic State Aid (BSA) formula. BSA base level increases for inflation also increase ASDB’s voucher funding. The Baseline increases the BSA base level by 2.0% for inflation in FY 2027, which will increase special education voucher funding into the ASDB Fund by an estimated \$244,900 in FY 2027.

Endowment Earnings Decrease

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(3,800) from the ASDB Fund in FY 2027 for decreased land trust endowment revenues.

When combined with the 2026 base adjustment of \$(1,442,100), the total ASDB Fund adjustment is \$(1,201,000). As a result, the Baseline decreases the ASDB Fund appropriation in FY 2027 by \$(1,201,000) to match forecasted revenues.

Background – Special education voucher monies in the ASDB Fund represent ASDB’s reimbursement from the Arizona Department of Education (ADE) for educational costs based on its enrollment. As with school districts, ASDB’s ADE funding is determined by statutory formula. These monies are deposited into the ASDB Fund. If enrollment is higher than anticipated, ADE will distribute additional funding to ASDB. These monies can be spent without a new appropriation, as ASDB is provided budget flexibility through an ongoing General Appropriation Act footnote. This line item includes funding for contracted specialized education services for preschool children who are blind.

School Bus/Agency Vehicle Replacement

The Baseline includes \$369,000 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for School Bus/Agency Vehicle Replacement. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item are used for the purchase of new school buses and agency vehicles. According to the Arizona Department of Administration - School Facilities Division rules for ASDB, a gasoline-powered bus should be replaced after 10 years or 150,000 miles. (Please see the FY 2022 Appropriations Report for more background).

Supplemental Early Childhood Therapies

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for supplemental early childhood therapies. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(100,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for supplemental early childhood therapies.

Cooperative Services

The Baseline includes \$15,346,300 from the Cooperative Services Fund in FY 2027 for Cooperative Services. Adjustments are as follows:

Base Adjustment

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(3,476,600) from the Cooperative Services Fund in FY 2027 for a base adjustment reflecting lower-than-anticipated revenues in comparison with the enacted budget. The FY 2026 enacted budget assumed the Cooperative Services Fund would receive total revenues of \$19,103,000 in FY 2026 from special education vouchers, membership fees, and tuition. The FY 2027 budget assumes that actual revenues into the Cooperative Services Fund in FY 2026 will be \$15,626,400, or \$(3,476,600) less than the appropriated amount. This base adjustment is mainly attributable to changes implemented by ASDB regarding the reimbursement of unexpended Special Education Voucher funding to participating school districts for students in ASDB regional cooperatives. Our estimate assumes that total enrollment in the ASDB regional cooperatives would remain unchanged from the October 2025 level of 752 in FY 2026.

Enrollment

The Baseline includes no net funding change from the Cooperative Services Fund in FY 2027 for enrollment. The budget assumes that enrollment of voucher students in regional cooperatives remains at the October 2025 level of 752, and therefore includes no funding increase or decrease for enrollment changes for ASDB's Cooperative Services Fund for FY 2027.

Revenue Decrease

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(280,100) from the Cooperative Services Fund in FY 2027 for estimated revenue adjustments, including:

An increase of \$389,700 for a 2.0% increase to the Base Level component of the Special Education Voucher formula. A.R.S. § 15-901.01 requires annual increases for inflation in the per pupil “base level” in the Basic State Aid (BSA) formula. BSA base level increases for inflation also increase ASDB’s voucher funding. The budget increases the BSA base level by 2.0% for inflation in FY 2027, which will increase special education voucher funding into the Cooperative Services Fund by an estimated \$389,700 in FY 2027.

A decrease of \$(669,800) in revenues from district membership fees, tuition receipts and Special Education Voucher reimbursement based on ASDB estimates of those revenue categories.

The Base Level and other revenue adjustments total to \$(280,100), and when combined with the base adjustment of \$(3,476,600), the total Cooperative Service Fund adjustment is \$(3,756,700). As a result, the Baseline decreases the Cooperative Services Fund appropriation in FY 2026 by \$(3,756,700) to match forecasted revenues.

Background – Regional Cooperatives provide services for deaf and blind students who are being served in a variety of settings in their home school district instead of an ASDB site-based program. Enrollment in ASDB's regional cooperatives as of October 2025 was 895.

The regional cooperatives, like ASDB's site-based programs, are funded by Special Education Vouchers paid by the Arizona Department of Education pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-1202. The program is also funded by tuition monies paid by participating districts as well as district membership fees.

Revenue Decrease

The monies in this line item represent the total estimated monies available for the program from vouchers, tuition, and district membership fees deposited in the Cooperative Services Fund. If available revenues exceed the original appropriation, a General Appropriations Act footnote stipulates that ASDB submit a report to JLBC detailing the intended use of the monies.

Cooperative Services Fund (SDA4221/A.R.S § 15-1202)

Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Revenues consist of tuition payments made by participating school districts or special education voucher monies claimed on their behalf by the Arizona School for the Deaf and Blind. Funds are used to support educational programs and supplemental services offered at the 3 state regional cooperatives. Purpose of Fund: To receive special education voucher monies paid to ASDB by the Department of Education on behalf of students enrolled in one of ASDB's 3 regional cooperatives, tuition payments from school districts, and district membership fees. Enterprise Fund (SDA4222/A.R.S. § 15-1323) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Monies received from fees, rentals, and other charges from the non-school use of facilities. Purpose of Fund: To defray the costs of operating those facilities (i.e. auditorium). Funds Expended 112,000 255,700 Year-End Fund Balance 505,800 411,000

Federal Grants (SDA2000/A.R.S. § 15-1303) Federal Funds

Source of Revenue: Federal Grants - Title I aid to schools; vocational rehabilitation; National School Lunch and Breakfast programs;   
Arizona deaf-blind project; preschool services; and Arizona Early Intervention program.

Instructional Improvement Fund (SDA2492/A.R.S. § 15-979) Non-Appropriated

Revenue Decrease

Source of Revenue: Shared revenue from Indian gaming, as authorized by Proposition 202 from the 2002 General Election. The Instructional Improvement Fund receives 56% of total shared revenue from Proposition 202. This is distributed among school districts, charter schools and ASDB based on student counts.

Non-Federal Grant Fund (SDA2011/A.R.S. § 15-1303) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Reimbursements from federal Rehabilitation Services Administration and E-rate programs, as well as grants from private corporations and other state agencies. Purpose of Fund: To reimburse ASDB for DSC-related expenditures and to accomplish specific projects of interest to the donor and ASDB. Funds Expended 456,600 386,500 Year-End Fund Balance 343,000 132,100

Schools for the Deaf and the Blind Fund (SDA2444/A.R.S. § 15-1304) Appropriated

Source of Revenue: "Special Education Fund" monies that ASDB receives from the Arizona Department of Education under the formula prescribed in A.R.S. § 15-1204. This formula is based on the number of pupils attending ASDB and the various special education "Group B" funding categories that those pupils qualify for under A.R.S. § 15-943(2b). This fund also receives expendable land endowment earnings pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-1304 and over-age and non-resident tuition income pursuant to A.R.S. § 15-1345. Purpose of Fund: To cover the cost of educating students receiving special education services at ASDB. Funds Expended 14,684,900 14,156,500 Year-End Fund Balance 3,141,700 1,883,300
